task_subtype: Small deterministic change, narrow transformation, or one-step answer
controller_model: Sonnet 5 or GPT-5.6 Terra; Opus 5 when failure cost is material
harness: Single agent with deterministic tools/tests
alternative_route: Opus 5 Medium solo
downshift_trigger: Clear acceptance test, low ambiguity, cheap rollback
escalation_trigger: Hidden coupling, failed test, unresolved requirement
verification_policy: Machine check or exact diff; no model-only self-approval
cost_latency_implications: Team overhead is likely negative; cheapest acceptable solo route
failure_modes: Unnecessary fan-out, context duplication, over-verification
revision_trigger: Representative local tasks show team reduces verified latency or severe failures

task_subtype: Contained autonomous patch with clear tests and bounded surface
harness: Claude Code / coding agent with tests
alternative_route: GPT-5.6 Sol High or Fable High for capability-sensitive tail
downshift_trigger: Mechanical change and strong tests -> Sonnet 5 High or Sol Medium
escalation_trigger: Architecture uncertainty, repeated failed patch, repo-wide root cause
verification_policy: Held-out tests, lint/typecheck, diff review; human review for consequential code
cost_latency_implications: Opus Medium is a strong efficiency point; higher effort can regress on FrontierCode
failure_modes: Scope expansion, redesign after a valid plan, redundant checks
revision_trigger: Local patch suite shows High/XHigh higher verified success at acceptable cost

task_subtype: Complex but tightly coupled architecture or debugging
solo_team_choice: Solo or one fresh verifier, not broad team
harness: Single lead plus bounded verifier
alternative_route: GPT-5.6 Sol High/XHigh; Fable High if work graph becomes dynamic
downshift_trigger: Root cause localized and testable
escalation_trigger: Competing plausible causes or repeated causal-model failure
verification_policy: Reproduce bug, invariant tests, adversarial regression tests
cost_latency_implications: XHigh only when the extra reasoning changes decisions; Max not default
failure_modes: Overthinking, tunnel vision, verifier correlation
revision_trigger: Paired debugging trials favor another model-effort combination

task_subtype: Independent source classes, jurisdictions, repositories, or hypotheses
context_topology: Isolated worker contexts; one synthesis context
worker_effort: Low/Medium for retrieval; High for interpretation
harness: Claude Code custom subagents or dynamic workflow
alternative_route: GPT-5.6 Sol multi-agent when homogeneous workers are acceptable
downshift_trigger: Fewer than three truly independent workstreams
escalation_trigger: Work graph changes, cross-worker dependencies emerge, project persists across rounds
verification_policy: Source-class coverage checklist, duplicate/contradiction detection, citation verifier
cost_latency_implications: Parallelism can reduce wall time but increases total tokens; cheap workers are usually sufficient
failure_modes: Duplicate searches, shallow summaries, synthesis omission
evidence_ids: P-O5 p163-168; P-F5 p270-276; W-CODE-SUBAGENTS; W-CODE-WORKFLOWS
revision_trigger: Controller-swap local eval shows Fable materially improves verified synthesis

task_subtype: Independent peers each receive full task and compare or merge results
solo_team_choice: Team only when diversity/replication is valuable
controller_model: Opus 5 or Fable 5 peers; deterministic merger
worker_model: Same model or mixed if harness supports
harness: Claude Code agent teams (experimental) or custom fixed peer harness
alternative_route: Subagents plus deterministic synthesis
downshift_trigger: Shared mutable files or sequential dependencies
escalation_trigger: Need direct peer debate or independent replication
verification_policy: Independent outputs before communication; conflict log; final machine check
cost_latency_implications: Linear token growth and diminishing returns; strong endpoints in vendor BrowseComp
failure_modes: Same-file conflicts, group convergence, redundant work
evidence_strength: Moderate for benchmark; low for production generalization
revision_trigger: Local repeated trials show stable gain after total-cost accounting

task_subtype: Lead dispatches one worker, waits, then continues
harness: Blocking supervisor-worker
alternative_route: Async long-lived subagents or solo lead
downshift_trigger: One side task only -> named subagent
escalation_trigger: Multiple independent workstreams or recurring worker context
verification_policy: Checkpoint after each return; preserve source/tool evidence
cost_latency_implications: Synchronization and repeated context establishment can dominate
failure_modes: Lead idle time, context restarts, long latency tail
revision_trigger: Operational constraints make async impossible and blocking proves reliable

task_subtype: Persistent research/engineering workers with repeated messages and evolving subtasks
context_topology: Long-lived isolated contexts + lead integration context
harness: Async Claude Code subagents with explicit checkpoints and messaging
concurrency_cap: 4 default; raise only with measured utilization
alternative_route: Opus 5 XHigh controller with same workers
downshift_trigger: Work graph stabilizes and worker communication becomes one-shot
escalation_trigger: Repeated replanning, cross-worker coordination, days-scale persistence
verification_policy: Tool-grounded status, worker deliverables, integration tests, fresh final verifier
cost_latency_implications: Fable controller premium can be offset by cheaper workers; long-lived context improves cache economics
failure_modes: Long turns, scope drift, fabricated progress, worker starvation
evidence_strength: Moderate vendor evidence; independent controller comparison missing
evidence_ids: P-F5 p270-276; W-A-FABLE sections Delegation/Parallel subagents; R-CLAW
revision_trigger: Same-worker controller swap finds Opus equal/better on verified cost or Fable premium fails to repay

task_subtype: Unknown work graph; streams created, merged, terminated as evidence arrives
context_topology: Evolving graph with selective shared state
controller_effort: XHigh; High as economic starting point
worker_model: Mixed: Opus 5 Medium/High, Sonnet 5 High, deterministic tools
harness: Fable lead + long-lived subagents; script-backed dynamic workflow for repeatable stages
alternative_route: Opus 5 XHigh + deterministic planner/workflow
downshift_trigger: Decomposition becomes stable and separable
escalation_trigger: Integrator repeatedly loses global objective or workers require active reallocation
verification_policy: Task graph audit, dependency checks, explicit stopping and rollback criteria
cost_latency_implications: Highest coordination overhead; use only when topology—not raw task difficulty—is the bottleneck
failure_modes: Runaway fan-out, stale plans, hidden dependencies, forgotten workstreams
recommendation_status: Provisional recommendation / speculation bounded by test
revision_trigger: Controlled dynamic-task suite reverses manager ranking

task_subtype: Independent repository areas with explicit interfaces
worker_effort: Medium implementers; High for ambiguous modules
harness: Custom subagents/worktrees; controller owns interface contract and merge
alternative_route: Fable High controller + same Opus workers for larger evolving migrations
downshift_trigger: One module or shared-file hot spot
escalation_trigger: Interfaces change repeatedly or integration failures dominate
verification_policy: Worker-local tests, API contract tests, integrated regression suite, human diff review
cost_latency_implications: Opus Medium workers exploit implementation sweet spot; avoid Fable workers unless tail capability is needed
failure_modes: Merge conflict, interface drift, duplicated refactors, weak integration
evidence_strength: Moderate for worker effort; low for controller choice
revision_trigger: Repo-scale paired trials show Fable controller reduces integration defects enough to repay cost

task_subtype: Multiple plausible root causes can be tested independently
coupling: Low during investigation, high at resolution
context_topology: Independent hypothesis contexts; shared evidence board
harness: Agent team or subagents with blind initial hypotheses
alternative_route: Fable High for repeated hypothesis generation/reallocation
downshift_trigger: Reproduction isolates one subsystem
escalation_trigger: Workers converge prematurely or evidence invalidates decomposition
verification_policy: Each worker must propose falsifier and execute test; integrator reruns decisive test
cost_latency_implications: Parallelism valuable only if tests are independent
failure_modes: Anchoring, correlated hypotheses, evidence cherry-picking
evidence_strength: Low-moderate; harness guidance, not model head-to-head
evidence_ids: W-CODE-TEAMS section competing hypotheses; P-O5 effort profiles
revision_trigger: Local debugging benchmark measures no benefit over solo

task_subtype: Draft plus independent factual/citation/acceptance verification
context_topology: Fresh verifier context with source packet
controller_effort: High for synthesis; Medium for bounded writing
worker_model: Sonnet 5 High, Opus 5 Medium, or GPT-5.6 Sol High as heterogeneous verifier
harness: Explicit writer -> verifier -> repair loop with capped retries
alternative_route: One Opus 5 Medium with deterministic checks when risk is low
downshift_trigger: All claims machine-verifiable and low consequence
escalation_trigger: Material contradictions, high-stakes decision, weak source coverage
verification_policy: Verifier sees acceptance criteria and primary evidence, not writer rationale; human adjudication for load-bearing disputes
cost_latency_implications: Fresh verification adds cost but is more defensible than broad swarm
failure_modes: Verifier deference, shared-family correlated error, endless repair loop
evidence_strength: Low-moderate; official guidance plus evaluation methodology
revision_trigger: Calibrated human sample shows verifier fails to catch severe errors

task_subtype: Code implementation then independent review/test attack
context_topology: Implementer repo context; reviewer fresh diff/test context
worker_model: Opus 5 Medium implementer + Sonnet 5 High or Sol High reviewer
harness: Subagents or separate sessions; reviewer cannot edit until findings logged
alternative_route: Opus 5 Medium solo with tests
downshift_trigger: Mechanical patch and exhaustive tests
escalation_trigger: Security, data migration, or architecture-sensitive change
verification_policy: Review checklist, hidden tests, mutation/adversarial tests; human approval for release
cost_latency_implications: Cheaper heterogenous reviewer may improve error diversity
failure_modes: Rubber-stamp review, shared blind spot, reviewer rewriting instead of testing
evidence_ids: P-O5 p151; W-CURSOR; AHR-C evaluation clauses
revision_trigger: Paired review experiment shows no severe-failure reduction

task_subtype: Stateful sequence where next action depends on prior tool result
harness: Single agent + explicit state machine / programmatic tool calling
alternative_route: Sonnet 5 High for routine low-risk flows
downshift_trigger: Deterministic graph can be scripted
escalation_trigger: Independent research branches appear
verification_policy: Read-after-write, idempotency, transaction log, external end-state check
cost_latency_implications: Multiple agents usually add overhead without parallel benefit
failure_modes: State loss, duplicate side effects, stale reads
evidence_strength: Moderate for architecture; model comparison low-moderate
revision_trigger: Local workflow trials show another route improves verified completion

task_subtype: Persistent evolving project with memory, worker lifecycle, checkpoints, and reprioritization
context_topology: Long-lived worker memories + external project ledger
controller_effort: High initially; XHigh on replanning/recovery checkpoints
worker_model: Mixed: Opus 5 Medium implementers, Sonnet 5 High scouts/reviewers, deterministic tools
worker_effort: Task-specific; keep routine work below XHigh
harness: Async lead + long-lived subagents + external task/memory system + scheduled verification gates
concurrency_cap: 4 active; queued backlog; explicit total worker budget
alternative_route: Opus 5 XHigh controller inside deterministic project-management scaffold
downshift_trigger: Project decomposes into stable work packages
escalation_trigger: Repeated missed dependencies, stalled workers, integration failures
verification_policy: Daily/phase evidence audit, acceptance tests, rollback checkpoints, human approval at irreversible gates
cost_latency_implications: Fable price premium is concentrated in controller; worker mix controls total spend; longest latency tails
failure_modes: False status, scope drift, forgotten dependencies, unbounded spend
evidence_strength: Low-moderate; vendor positioning and harness guidance
revision_trigger: 30-task local longitudinal pilot shows no coordination advantage or unacceptable refusal/availability burden

task_subtype: Same model and effort for lead and workers
solo_team_choice: Use for clean benchmark comparison or simple deployment
controller_effort: Match worker effort only when experiment requires
harness: Vendor-style fixed/async team
alternative_route: Mixed team that separates controller and worker economics
downshift_trigger: Worker tasks are routine
escalation_trigger: Worker capability is the bottleneck
verification_policy: Report lead and worker effort separately; preserve failures
cost_latency_implications: Simple but confounds controller and worker quality; expensive with Fable
failure_modes: Cannot attribute gain, correlated errors, needless premium workers
revision_trigger: Published controller-swap study resolves attribution

task_subtype: Premium controller + efficient implementation workers
context_topology: Manager context plus task-specialized worker contexts
worker_effort: Medium implementers; High for ambiguous modules
harness: Claude Code custom subagents with per-worker model/effort overrides
alternative_route: Opus 5 High controller + same workers
downshift_trigger: Controller spends most time doing implementation rather than organization
escalation_trigger: Work graph churn, cross-worker communication, integration defects
verification_policy: Controller cannot mark worker task done without tests/evidence; independent final verifier
cost_latency_implications: Economic hypothesis: buy Fable only for management tokens; not publicly validated head-to-head
failure_modes: Manager overreach, workers under-scoped, integration blind spot
evidence_strength: Low; plausible mixed policy, not controlled public result
revision_trigger: Controller-isolation A/B shows cost per verified success is worse than Opus controller

task_subtype: Strong controller + low-cost scouts / breadth workers
harness: Custom subagents or cross-provider workflow
alternative_route: GPT-5.6 Sol multi-agent homogeneous
downshift_trigger: Retrieval volume small
escalation_trigger: Workers must make high-stakes interpretive judgments
verification_policy: Controller samples primary sources; deterministic dedupe and citation checks
cost_latency_implications: Largest cost savings when worker volume dominates; cross-provider integration adds engineering/privacy burden
failure_modes: Cheap-worker omissions, inconsistent formats, transport friction
revision_trigger: Trace replay shows quality loss outweighs savings

task_subtype: Consequential factual synthesis with contradictory evidence
harness: Bounded fan-out + writer-verifier + human sign-off
alternative_route: GPT-5.6 Sol High/XHigh with same controls
downshift_trigger: Low consequence and direct primary evidence
escalation_trigger: Material disagreement, legal/financial/safety consequence, unresolved citations
verification_policy: Claim-level source links, calculation audit, human validation of load-bearing judgments
cost_latency_implications: Verification burden dominates model price; optimize cost per acceptable verified result
failure_modes: Citation laundering, false consensus, correlated model judges
revision_trigger: User risk tolerance or authoritative evidence changes

task_subtype: One coherent corpus with global dependencies and little parallelism
controller_model: Opus 5 or GPT-5.6 Sol; Fable for extreme ambiguity
harness: Single long-context agent with indexed evidence
alternative_route: Fable High/XHigh for multithreaded ambiguity
downshift_trigger: Corpus can be partitioned without cross-links
escalation_trigger: Context exceeds reliable recall or contradictory source classes require independent checks
verification_policy: Evidence map, retrieval recall checks, source citations
cost_latency_implications: Parallel agents duplicate corpus tokens; long-input pricing/caching matters
failure_modes: Lost cross-document dependency, context dilution, expensive duplication
revision_trigger: Local long-context retrieval tests show stable superiority

task_subtype: Documents, spreadsheets, slides, visual QA, or computer-use refinement
solo_team_choice: Solo creator plus verifier; avoid broad team
controller_model: GPT-5.6 Sol or Opus 5; Fable for complex enterprise bundles
worker_model: Sonnet 5 / Sol Terra for extraction or QA
harness: Artifact toolchain with render-and-verify loop
alternative_route: Fable High for long-running multithreaded enterprise workflow
downshift_trigger: Template fill or simple transformation
escalation_trigger: Many linked artifacts, contradictory source data, repeated visual defects
verification_policy: Render/open every artifact; formula/link/reference validation
cost_latency_implications: Sol has strong current vendor/practitioner evidence for artifacts; harness matters more than raw model
failure_modes: Polished but wrong output, broken formulas, layout defects
revision_trigger: Representative artifact suite with blinded human scoring changes ranking
